title: Remove inert runner package-lock stub
goal: Delete the 6-line stub file runner/package-lock.json (an empty packages object with no matching runner/package.json to anchor it). Three separate reviews of task b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd confirmed it is inert: no script, Dockerfile step, or publish step installs from it, and the runner test suites pass with it present. It is almost certainly an accidental npm artifact and its presence confuses agents auditing the runner packaging path. Acceptance: the stub file is gone, the runner packaging script and both runner test suites still pass, and no reference to the stub remains in scripts or docs. Case-study reference: task b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd, where the stub was flagged in the update-impact review, the PR review, and the final re-verification but left in place as out of scope.

Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

+# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
+
+Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
+Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
+
+## Goal
+
+Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
+object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
+auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
+artifact.
+
+## Success Criteria
+
+1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
+2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
+3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
+   definition).
+4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
+   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
+5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
+   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
+
+## Context and grounded facts
+
+- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
+  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
+- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
+  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
+- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
+  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
+  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
+  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
+  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
+- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
+  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
+  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
+  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
+- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
+  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
+  contain no reference to the stub.
+- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
+  left in place as out of scope —
+  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
+  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
+  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
+  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
+  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
+  `node --check runner/project.js` and
+  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
+  with the stub present.
+- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
+  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
+  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
+  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
+  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
+  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
+  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
+  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
+
+## Key decisions
+
+1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
+   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
+   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
+   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
+   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
+   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
+   intended.
+2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
+   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
+   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
+   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
+   `docs/tasks/`.
+3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
+   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
+   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
+   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
+   tarball behavior.
+
+## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
+
+Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
+"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
+green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
+delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
+is a single step near the end.
+
+## Steps
+
+### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
+
+1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
+reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):
+expect hits only in `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` (historical, ignored per Key
+Decision 2) and zero hits in `scripts/`, `runner/`, `Dockerfile`,

+# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
+
+Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
+Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
+
+## Goal
+
+Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
+object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
+auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
+artifact.
+
+## Success Criteria
+
+1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
+2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
+3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
+   definition).
+4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
+   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
+5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
+   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
+
+## Context and grounded facts
+
+- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
+  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
+- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
+  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
+- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
+  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
+  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
+  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
+  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
+- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
+  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
+  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
+  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
+- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
+  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
+  contain no reference to the stub.
+- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
+  left in place as out of scope —
+  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
+  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
+  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
+  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
+  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
+  `node --check runner/project.js` and
+  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
+  with the stub present.
+- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
+  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
+  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
+  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
+  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
+  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
+  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
+  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
+
+## Key decisions
+
+1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
+   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
+   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
+   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
+   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
+   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
+   intended.
+2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
+   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
+   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
+   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
+   `docs/tasks/`.
+3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
+   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
+   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
+   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
+   tarball behavior.
+
+## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
+
+Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
+"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
+green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
+delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
+is a single step near the end.
+
+## Steps
+
+### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
+
+1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
+reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):
+expect hits only in `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` (historical, ignored per Key
+Decision 2) and zero hits in `scripts/`, `runner/`, `Dockerfile`,
+`publish.sh`, `startRunner.sh`, `tests/`, and live `docs/`.
+Suggested commands (run from the repo root):
+`grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`
+and `grep -rn "package-lock" runner/ scripts/package-runner.* Dockerfile publish.sh`.
+
+1.2. **Install-step audit.** Confirm no step installs from the runner tree:
+search for `--prefix runner` across shell scripts, `.mjs`/`.js` files, and
+the `Dockerfile`; confirm `scripts/package-runner.mjs` reads only
+`api/package-lock.json`, and the `Dockerfile` copies only `api/` and
+`frontend/` lockfiles.
+
+1.3. **Manifest-absence check.** Confirm `runner/package.json` still does not
+exist (`ls runner/package.json` fails) and `runner/version.json` is the only
+runner metadata the packager reads.
+
+1.4. **Conformance-test review.** Skim `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`
+to confirm no assertion pins the stub's presence in the tarball (current
+assertions cover build stamps and layout, not an exact file list — re-confirm
+at implementation time in case the file changed).
+
+### Phase 2 — Green baseline (before touching anything)
+
+2.1. **Run the cited runner pair** and record the pass count (expect 182/182
+per the case study, or the current count if suites grew):
+`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`
+
+2.2. **Run the full `Unit Tests (runner)` branch** — all 20 files named in
+`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`runner/ciBranchWorkdir.test.js`,
+`runner/daemon.test.js`, `runner/client.test.js`,
+`runner/impromptu.test.js`, `runner/config.test.js`,
+`runner/gitOps.test.js`, `runner/harness.test.js`,
+`runner/logEvents.test.js`, `runner/modelDiscovery.test.js`,
+`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js`, `runner/project.test.js`, plus the
+nine `runner/updates-*.test.js` files). Use the exact file list from
+`buildBranches` (or the equivalent `publish.sh --runner` test gate); all must
+pass.
+
+2.3. **Run the runner packaging script** and record success plus the stub's
+presence in the output:
+`bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check`
+then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-baseline-stub-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
+(expect one hit — proof the stub currently ships as inert bytes).
+`dist/` is gitignored, so the tarball does not dirty the tree; delete it
+after inspection to keep the workspace tidy.
+
+2.4. **Run the packaging-related harness tests** as a baseline:
+`node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs`
+
+### Phase 3 — The change
+
+3.1. **Delete the stub with git** so the removal is staged explicitly:
+`git rm runner/package-lock.json`
+Then `git status --short` must show exactly one change: the deletion.
+
+### Phase 4 — Post-deletion verification
+
+4.1. **Re-run the reference sweep** (same commands as 1.1–1.2). Live-tree
+hits must be zero; only the `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` historical mentions
+remain.
+
+4.2. **Re-run the cited runner pair** (`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`):
+must pass with the identical count as the Phase 2 baseline.
+
+4.3. **Re-run the full 20-file `Unit Tests (runner)` branch**: all must pass.
+
+4.4. **Re-run the packaging script**:
+`bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check`
+then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-post-delete-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
+(expect no hits — proof the tarball no longer carries the stub) and confirm
+the tarball still contains `runner/`, `api/`, `shared/`, and both
+`version.json` copies. Delete the scratch tarballs afterwards.
+
+4.5. **Re-run the packaging-related harness tests** (same list as 2.4): all
+must pass.
+
+4.6. **Final tree check**: `git status --short` shows only the deletion;
+`git diff --stat` shows one file removed. No `dist/` artifacts, no stray
+files.
+
+## Validation plan (evidence-oriented)
+
+| Check | Command | Expected evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| Cited pair, before + after | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` | Identical pass counts, 0 failures, both runs |
+| Full runner branch, before + after | `node --test` with the 20 files from `buildBranches` | All pass, both runs |
+| Packaging, before | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball contains `runner/package-lock.json` |
+| Packaging, after | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball omits the stub, keeps `runner/` + `version.json` copies |
+| Harness packaging tests, before + after | `node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs` | All pass, both runs |
+| Reference sweep, before + after | `grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` | Before: only `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` hits. After: same, zero live hits |
+| Tree cleanliness | `git status --short` / `git diff --stat` | Exactly one deleted file |
+
+The highest-risk validation step is **packaging after deletion (4.4)** — the
+only step whose outcome cannot be fully predicted from the audit, since it
+exercises the real tar + npm-closure path. If it fails, stop and diagnose
+before claiming success; do not wave it through on the strength of the unit
+suites.
+
+Manual check that cannot be automated: open the before/after `tar -tzf`
+listings side by side and confirm the *only* entry difference is the missing
+`runner/package-lock.json` line.
+
+## Documentation plan
+
+- **No live-doc edits are expected.** The audit found no live doc referencing
+  the stub, so the implementation should change zero docs. If the Phase 1
+  sweep surfaces a live reference, update or remove that mention and run
+  `npm run docs:check` (link + JSDoc-example gates) to prove the docs tree is
+  still consistent.
+- **Historical reports stay untouched.** Do not edit the `b31cab50` review
+  files or this plan's survey/idea inputs.
+- **This plan file** (`docs/tasks/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`)
+  is the stage deliverable; no other docs artifact is required.
+
+## Risks and open questions
+
+- **Risk (low): a hidden consumer of the stub.** Mitigated by the Phase 1
+  sweep plus the before/after packaging diff; the manifest-absence check
+  makes an npm consumer impossible by construction.
+- **Risk (low): suite-count drift.** The 182/182 figure is from the case
+  study; suites may have grown since. The plan handles this by comparing
+  before/after counts rather than pinning 182.
+- **Risk (negligible): `dist/` pollution.** `dist/` is gitignored; scratch
+  tarballs are deleted in steps 2.3 and 4.4 regardless.
+- **Open questions: none.** The survey recorded no concerns, and every
+  material fact (stub content, missing manifest, no install step, no live
+  references, packaging behavior) was verified against the checkout. The only
+  assumption is Key Decision 1's reading of "both runner test suites", which
+  the plan covers by running both the cited pair and the full branch.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- No changes to the packager, Dockerfile, publish flow, or any test.
+- No new regression test asserting the file's absence (see Key Decision 3).
+- No cleanup of other cruft, no `.gitignore` additions, no version bump
+  (`runner/version.json` is untouched — this is not a runner release).

+# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
+
+Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
+Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
+
+## Goal
+
+Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
+object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
+auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
+artifact.
+
+## Success Criteria
+
+1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
+2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
+3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
+   definition).
+4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
+   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
+5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
+   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
+
+## Context and grounded facts
+
+- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
+  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
+- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
+  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
+- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
+  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
+  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
+  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
+  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
+- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
+  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
+  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
+  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
+- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
+  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
+  contain no reference to the stub.
+- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
+  left in place as out of scope —
+  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
+  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
+  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
+  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
+  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
+  `node --check runner/project.js` and
+  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
+  with the stub present.
+- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
+  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
+  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
+  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
+  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
+  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
+  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
+  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
+
+## Key decisions
+
+1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
+   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
+   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
+   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
+   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
+   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
+   intended.
+2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
+   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
+   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
+   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
+   `docs/tasks/`.
+3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
+   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
+   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
+   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
+   tarball behavior.
+
+## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
+
+Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
+"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
+green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
+delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
+is a single step near the end.
+
+## Steps
+
+### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
+
+1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
+reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):
+expect hits only in `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` (historical, ignored per Key
+Decision 2) and zero hits in `scripts/`, `runner/`, `Dockerfile`,
+`publish.sh`, `startRunner.sh`, `tests/`, and live `docs/`.
+Suggested commands (run from the repo root):
+`grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`
+and `grep -rn "package-lock" runner/ scripts/package-runner.* Dockerfile publish.sh`.
+
+1.2. **Install-step audit.** Confirm no step installs from the runner tree:
+search for `--prefix runner` across shell scripts, `.mjs`/`.js` files, and
+the `Dockerfile`; confirm `scripts/package-runner.mjs` reads only
+`api/package-lock.json`, and the `Dockerfile` copies only `api/` and
+`frontend/` lockfiles.
+
+1.3. **Manifest-absence check.** Confirm `runner/package.json` still does not
+exist (`ls runner/package.json` fails) and `runner/version.json` is the only
+runner metadata the packager reads.
+
+1.4. **Conformance-test review.** Skim `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`
+to confirm no assertion pins the stub's presence in the tarball (current
+assertions cover build stamps and layout, not an exact file list — re-confirm
+at implementation time in case the file changed).
+
+### Phase 2 — Green baseline (before touching anything)
+
+2.1. **Run the cited runner pair** and record the pass count (expect 182/182
+per the case study, or the current count if suites grew):
+`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`
+
+2.2. **Run the full `Unit Tests (runner)` branch** — all 20 files named in
+`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`runner/ciBranchWorkdir.test.js`,
+`runner/daemon.test.js`, `runner/client.test.js`,
+`runner/impromptu.test.js`, `runner/config.test.js`,
+`runner/gitOps.test.js`, `runner/harness.test.js`,
+`runner/logEvents.test.js`, `runner/modelDiscovery.test.js`,
+`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js`, `runner/project.test.js`, plus the
+nine `runner/updates-*.test.js` files). Use the exact file list from
+`buildBranches` (or the equivalent `publish.sh --runner` test gate); all must
+pass.
+
+2.3. **Run the runner packaging script** and record success plus the stub's
+presence in the output:
+`bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check`
+then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-baseline-stub-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
+(expect one hit — proof the stub currently ships as inert bytes).
+`dist/` is gitignored, so the tarball does not dirty the tree; delete it
+after inspection to keep the workspace tidy.
+
+2.4. **Run the packaging-related harness tests** as a baseline:
+`node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs`
+
+### Phase 3 — The change
+
+3.1. **Delete the stub with git** so the removal is staged explicitly:
+`git rm runner/package-lock.json`
+Then `git status --short` must show exactly one change: the deletion.
+
+### Phase 4 — Post-deletion verification
+
+4.1. **Re-run the reference sweep** (same commands as 1.1–1.2). Live-tree
+hits must be zero; only the `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` historical mentions
+remain.
+
+4.2. **Re-run the cited runner pair** (`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`):
+must pass with the identical count as the Phase 2 baseline.
+
+4.3. **Re-run the full 20-file `Unit Tests (runner)` branch**: all must pass.
+
+4.4. **Re-run the packaging script**:
+`bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check`
+then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-post-delete-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
+(expect no hits — proof the tarball no longer carries the stub) and confirm
+the tarball still contains `runner/`, `api/`, `shared/`, and both
+`version.json` copies. Delete the scratch tarballs afterwards.
+
+4.5. **Re-run the packaging-related harness tests** (same list as 2.4): all
+must pass.
+
+4.6. **Final tree check**: `git status --short` shows only the deletion;
+`git diff --stat` shows one file removed. No `dist/` artifacts, no stray
+files.
+
+## Validation plan (evidence-oriented)
+
+| Check | Command | Expected evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| Cited pair, before + after | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` | Identical pass counts, 0 failures, both runs |
+| Full runner branch, before + after | `node --test` with the 20 files from `buildBranches` | All pass, both runs |
+| Packaging, before | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball contains `runner/package-lock.json` |
+| Packaging, after | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball omits the stub, keeps `runner/` + `version.json` copies |
+| Harness packaging tests, before + after | `node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs` | All pass, both runs |
+| Reference sweep, before + after | `grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` | Before: only `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` hits. After: same, zero live hits |
+| Tree cleanliness | `git status --short` / `git diff --stat` | Exactly one deleted file |
+
+The highest-risk validation step is **packaging after deletion (4.4)** — the
+only step whose outcome cannot be fully predicted from the audit, since it
+exercises the real tar + npm-closure path. If it fails, stop and diagnose
+before claiming success; do not wave it through on the strength of the unit
+suites.
+
+Manual check that cannot be automated: open the before/after `tar -tzf`
+listings side by side and confirm the *only* entry difference is the missing
+`runner/package-lock.json` line.
+
+## Documentation plan
+
+- **No live-doc edits are expected.** The audit found no live doc referencing
+  the stub, so the implementation should change zero docs. If the Phase 1
+  sweep surfaces a live reference, update or remove that mention and run
+  `npm run docs:check` (link + JSDoc-example gates) to prove the docs tree is
+  still consistent.
+- **Historical reports stay untouched.** Do not edit the `b31cab50` review
+  files or this plan's survey/idea inputs.
+- **This plan file** (`docs/tasks/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`)
+  is the stage deliverable; no other docs artifact is required.
+
+## Risks and open questions
+
+- **Risk (low): a hidden consumer of the stub.** Mitigated by the Phase 1
+  sweep plus the before/after packaging diff; the manifest-absence check
+  makes an npm consumer impossible by construction.
+- **Risk (low): suite-count drift.** The 182/182 figure is from the case
+  study; suites may have grown since. The plan handles this by comparing
+  before/after counts rather than pinning 182.
+- **Risk (negligible): `dist/` pollution.** `dist/` is gitignored; scratch
+  tarballs are deleted in steps 2.3 and 4.4 regardless.
+- **Open questions: none.** The survey recorded no concerns, and every
+  material fact (stub content, missing manifest, no install step, no live
+  references, packaging behavior) was verified against the checkout. The only
+  assumption is Key Decision 1's reading of "both runner test suites", which
+  the plan covers by running both the cited pair and the full branch.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- No changes to the packager, Dockerfile, publish flow, or any test.
+- No new regression test asserting the file's absence (see Key Decision 3).
+- No cleanup of other cruft, no `.gitignore` additions, no version bump
+  (`runner/version.json` is untouched — this is not a runner release).

+## Key decisions
+
+1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
+   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
+   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
+   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
+   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
+   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
+   intended.
+2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
+   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
+   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
+   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
+   `docs/tasks/`.
+3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
+   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
+   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
+   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
+   tarball behavior.
+
+## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
+
+Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
+"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
+green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
+delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
+is a single step near the end.

+1.2. **Install-step audit.** Confirm no step installs from the runner tree:

+# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
+
+Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
+Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
+
+## Goal
+
+Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
+object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
+auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
+artifact.
+
+## Success Criteria
+
+1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
+2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
+3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
+   definition).
+4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
+   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
+5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
+   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
+
+## Context and grounded facts
+
+- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
+  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
+- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
+  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
+- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
+  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
+  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
+  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
+  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
+- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
+  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
+  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
+  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
+- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
+  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
+  contain no reference to the stub.
+- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
+  left in place as out of scope —
+  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
+  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
+  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
+  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
+  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
+  `node --check runner/project.js` and
+  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
+  with the stub present.
+- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
+  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
+  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
+  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
+  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
+  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
+  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
+  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
+
+## Key decisions
+
+1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
+   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
+   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
+   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
+   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
+   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
+   intended.
+2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
+   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
+   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
+   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
+   `docs/tasks/`.
+3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
+   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
+   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
+   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
+   tarball behavior.
+
+## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
+
+Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
+"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
+green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
+delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
+is a single step near the end.
+
+## Steps
+
+### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
+
+1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
+reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):

+  install from a lockfile with no manifest.

+  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
+  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
+  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
+  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).

+  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
+  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
+  bytes; no packager logic names the file.

+  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
+  contain no reference to the stub.

+  left in place as out of scope —

Read text file `docs/tasks/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
2|
3|Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
4|Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
5|
6|## Goal
7|
8|Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
9|object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
10|auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
11|artifact.
12|
13|## Success Criteria
14|
15|1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
16|2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
17|3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
18|   definition).
19|4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
20|   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
21|5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
22|   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
23|
24|## Context and grounded facts
25|
26|- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
27|  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
28|- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
29|  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
30|- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
31|  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
32|  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
33|  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
34|  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
35|- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
36|  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
37|  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
38|  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
39|- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
40|  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
41|  contain no reference to the stub.
42|- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
43|  left in place as out of scope —
44|  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
45|  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
46|  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
47|  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
48|  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
49|  `node --check runner/project.js` and
50|  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
51|  with the stub present.
52|- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
53|  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
54|  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
55|  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
56|  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
57|  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
58|  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
59|  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
60|
61|## Key decisions
62|
63|1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
64|   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
65|   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
66|   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
67|   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
68|   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
69|   intended.
70|2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
71|   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
72|   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
73|   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
74|   `docs/tasks/`.
75|3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
76|   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
77|   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
78|   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
79|   tarball behavior.
80|
81|## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
82|
83|Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
84|"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
85|green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
86|delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
87|is a single step near the end.
88|
89|## Steps
90|
91|### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
92|
93|1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
94|reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):
95|expect hits only in `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` (historical, ignored per Key
96|Decision 2) and zero hits in `scripts/`, `runner/`, `Dockerfile`,
97|`publish.sh`, `startRunner.sh`, `tests/`, and live `docs/`.
98|Suggested commands (run from the repo root):
99|`grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`
100|and `grep -rn "package-lock" runner/ scripts/package-runner.* Dockerfile publish.sh`.
101|
102|1.2. **Install-step audit.** Confirm no step installs from the runner tree:
103|search for `--prefix runner` across shell scripts, `.mjs`/`.js` files, and
104|the `Dockerfile`; confirm `scripts/package-runner.mjs` reads only
105|`api/package-lock.json`, and the `Dockerfile` copies only `api/` and
106|`frontend/` lockfiles.
107|
108|1.3. **Manifest-absence check.** Confirm `runner/package.json` still does not
109|exist (`ls runner/package.json` fails) and `runner/version.json` is the only
110|runner metadata the packager reads.
111|
112|1.4. **Conformance-test review.** Skim `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`
113|to confirm no assertion pins the stub's presence in the tarball (current
114|assertions cover build stamps and layout, not an exact file list — re-confirm
115|at implementation time in case the file changed).
116|
117|### Phase 2 — Green baseline (before touching anything)
118|
119|2.1. **Run the cited runner pair** and record the pass count (expect 182/182
120|per the case study, or the current count if suites grew):
121|`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`
122|
123|2.2. **Run the full `Unit Tests (runner)` branch** — all 20 files named in
124|`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`runner/ciBranchWorkdir.test.js`,
125|`runner/daemon.test.js`, `runner/client.test.js`,
126|`runner/impromptu.test.js`, `runner/config.test.js`,
127|`runner/gitOps.test.js`, `runner/harness.test.js`,
128|`runner/logEvents.test.js`, `runner/modelDiscovery.test.js`,
129|`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js`, `runner/project.test.js`, plus the
130|nine `runner/updates-*.test.js` files). Use the exact file list from
131|`buildBranches` (or the equivalent `publish.sh --runner` test gate); all must
132|pass.
133|
134|2.3. **Run the runner packaging script** and record success plus the stub's
135|presence in the output:
136|`bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check`

1|# Implementation Plan — Delete the `runner/package-lock.json` stub
2|
3|Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
4|Case-study reference: task `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd`
5|
6|## Goal
7|
8|Delete the 6-line stub file `runner/package-lock.json` (an empty `packages`
9|object with no matching `runner/package.json` to anchor it), so agents
10|auditing the runner packaging path stop tripping over an inert accidental npm
11|artifact.
12|
13|## Success Criteria
14|
15|1. `runner/package-lock.json` no longer exists in the working tree.
16|2. The runner packaging script still builds a valid distributable tarball.
17|3. Both runner test suites still pass (see Key Decision 1 for the exact
18|   definition).
19|4. No reference to the stub remains in live scripts or live docs (see Key
20|   Decision 2 for the historical-docs exception).
21|5. The final diff contains only the deletion — no source, config, or
22|   test edits (`runner/` stays non-empty, so no directory cleanup applies).
23|
24|## Context and grounded facts
25|
26|- Stub content (verified in this checkout): 6 lines / 85 bytes —
27|  `{"name": "runner", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true, "packages": {}}`.
28|- `runner/package.json` does not exist (verified: `ls` fails). Nothing can
29|  install from a lockfile with no manifest.
30|- No install step targets the runner tree: a repo-wide search finds no
31|  `npm ci --prefix runner` / `npm install --prefix runner` in any script,
32|  `Dockerfile` step, or publish step. The only lockfiles the build reads are
33|  `api/package-lock.json` (pinned by `scripts/package-runner.mjs` for the
34|  discovery-leg closure) and `frontend/package-lock.json` (Dockerfile).
35|- The packager (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `copyPruned`) copies the whole
36|  `runner/` tree except forbidden basenames/suffixes, so the stub currently
37|  ships inside the tarball as inert bytes. Deleting it only removes those
38|  bytes; no packager logic names the file.
39|- The `Dockerfile` never mentions `runner/` lockfiles (only `api/` and
40|  `frontend/` ones). `runner/README.md` and `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`
41|  contain no reference to the stub.
42|- Case-study evidence (`b31cab50`): the stub was flagged in three reviews and
43|  left in place as out of scope —
44|  `docs/tasks/b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd/update-impact-20261116.md`
45|  (line 39: "cruft worth removing in a follow-up"),
46|  `pr-review-20261116.md` (lines 92–94: "looks like an accidental `npm`
47|  artifact; remove it"), and `pr-review-20261116-final.md` (lines 77–79:
48|  "inert cruft worth removing"). The update-impact review recorded
49|  `node --check runner/project.js` and
50|  `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` (182/182) passing
51|  with the stub present.
52|- Survey input (`SURVEY.md`, recovered from
53|  `origin/kb/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403` commit `430e3636`): the
54|  question-me round asked a single question — "I think this is simple enough
55|  to not require questions. Do you agree?" ("Yes - just delete the unused
56|  file" / "No - I have concerns") — and recorded no answers and no concerns.
57|  This plan therefore keeps the change minimal (a pure deletion, no new
58|  abstractions, no follow-up refactors) while retaining the verification
59|  below, since "simple" still deserves proof of inertness.
60|
61|## Key decisions
62|
63|1. **"Both runner test suites" means, at minimum, `runner/daemon.test.js` +
64|   `runner/project.test.js`** (the pair the case-study review ran, 182/182).
65|   Because the full `Unit Tests (runner)` gate branch runs 20 files
66|   (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `buildBranches`), the plan runs the cited pair
67|   first and then the full 20-file branch, so every reading of "both suites"
68|   is covered. Assumption, stated explicitly: no narrower suite pair is
69|   intended.
70|2. **Historical task reports are out of scope for the "no reference remains"
71|   sweep.** The three `b31cab50` review files name the stub as audit evidence;
72|   they are immutable history and must not be edited. The acceptance sweep
73|   covers live scripts, live docs, and tests — i.e. everything except
74|   `docs/tasks/`.
75|3. **Pure deletion, no hardening.** No `.gitignore` entry, no packager
76|   assertion, and no regression test are added: a test that asserts a file
77|   does *not* exist adds no value (any future accidental `npm` artifact would
78|   have a different shape), and the existing conformance tests already pin
79|   tarball behavior.
80|
81|## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
82|
83|Because the change itself is one deletion, almost all the work is the
84|"make it easy" half: prove the file is inert (reference sweep), capture a
85|green baseline (packaging + suites pass *before* the deletion), and only then
86|delete and re-prove. Research and evidence gathering come first; the deletion
87|is a single step near the end.
88|
89|## Steps
90|
91|### Phase 1 — Pre-deletion inertness audit (research; biggest piece first)
92|
93|1.1. **Repo-wide reference sweep for the stub.** Search for every live
94|reference to `runner/package-lock` (and bare `package-lock` under `runner/`):
95|expect hits only in `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` (historical, ignored per Key
96|Decision 2) and zero hits in `scripts/`, `runner/`, `Dockerfile`,
97|`publish.sh`, `startRunner.sh`, `tests/`, and live `docs/`.
98|Suggested commands (run from the repo root):
99|`grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .`
100|and `grep -rn "package-lock" runner/ scripts/package-runner.* Dockerfile publish.sh`.
101|
102|1.2. **Install-step audit.** Confirm no step installs from the runner tree:
103|search for `--prefix runner` across shell scripts, `.mjs`/`.js` files, and
104|the `Dockerfile`; confirm `scripts/package-runner.mjs` reads only
105|`api/package-lock.json`, and the `Dockerfile` copies only `api/` and
106|`frontend/` lockfiles.
107|
108|1.3. **Manifest-absence check.** Confirm `runner/package.json` still does not
109|exist (`ls runner/package.json` fails) and `runner/version.json` is the only
110|runner metadata the packager reads.
111|
112|1.4. **Conformance-test review.** Skim `tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs`
113|to confirm no assertion pins the stub's presence in the tarball (current
114|assertions cover build stamps and layout, not an exact file list — re-confirm
115|at implementation time in case the file changed).
116|
117|### Phase 2 — Green baseline (before touching anything)
118|
119|2.1. **Run the cited runner pair** and record the pass count (expect 182/182
120|per the case study, or the current count if suites grew):
121|`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`
122|
123|2.2. **Run the full `Unit Tests (runner)` branch** — all 20 files named in
124|`scripts/run-tests.mjs` (`runner/ciBranchWorkdir.test.js`,
125|`runner/daemon.test.js`, `runner/client.test.js`,
126|`runner/impromptu.test.js`, `runner/config.test.js`,
127|`runner/gitOps.test.js`, `runner/harness.test.js`,
128|`runner/logEvents.test.js`, `runner/modelDiscovery.test.js`,
129|`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js`, `runner/project.test.js`, plus the
130|nine `runner/updates-*.test.js` files). Use the exact file list from
131|`buildBranches` (or the equivalent `publish.sh --runner` test gate); all must
132|pass.
133|
134|2.3. **Run the runner packaging script** and record success plus the stub's
135|presence in the output:
136|`bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check`
137|then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-baseline-stub-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
138|(expect one hit — proof the stub currently ships as inert bytes).
139|`dist/` is gitignored, so the tarball does not dirty the tree; delete it
140|after inspection to keep the workspace tidy.
141|
142|2.4. **Run the packaging-related harness tests** as a baseline:
143|`node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs`
144|
145|### Phase 3 — The change
146|
147|3.1. **Delete the stub with git** so the removal is staged explicitly:
148|`git rm runner/package-lock.json`
149|Then `git status --short` must show exactly one change: the deletion.
150|
151|### Phase 4 — Post-deletion verification
152|
153|4.1. **Re-run the reference sweep** (same commands as 1.1–1.2). Live-tree
154|hits must be zero; only the `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` historical mentions
155|remain.
156|
157|4.2. **Re-run the cited runner pair** (`node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js`):
158|must pass with the identical count as the Phase 2 baseline.
159|
160|4.3. **Re-run the full 20-file `Unit Tests (runner)` branch**: all must pass.
161|
162|4.4. **Re-run the packaging script**:
163|`bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check`
164|then `tar -tzf dist/kainbain-runner-post-delete-check.tar.gz | grep "runner/package-lock.json"`
165|(expect no hits — proof the tarball no longer carries the stub) and confirm
166|the tarball still contains `runner/`, `api/`, `shared/`, and both
167|`version.json` copies. Delete the scratch tarballs afterwards.
168|
169|4.5. **Re-run the packaging-related harness tests** (same list as 2.4): all
170|must pass.
171|
172|4.6. **Final tree check**: `git status --short` shows only the deletion;
173|`git diff --stat` shows one file removed. No `dist/` artifacts, no stray
174|files.
175|
176|## Validation plan (evidence-oriented)
177|
178|| Check | Command | Expected evidence |
179||---|---|---|
180|| Cited pair, before + after | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js runner/project.test.js` | Identical pass counts, 0 failures, both runs |
181|| Full runner branch, before + after | `node --test` with the 20 files from `buildBranches` | All pass, both runs |
182|| Packaging, before | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh baseline-stub-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball contains `runner/package-lock.json` |
183|| Packaging, after | `bash scripts/package-runner.sh post-delete-check` + `tar -tzf` grep | Build succeeds; tarball omits the stub, keeps `runner/` + `version.json` copies |
184|| Harness packaging tests, before + after | `node --test tests/package-runner-conformance.test.mjs tests/runner-release-manifest.test.mjs tests/check-runner-version-bump.test.mjs tests/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.test.mjs tests/install-runner-wrapper.test.mjs` | All pass, both runs |
185|| Reference sweep, before + after | `grep -rn "runner/package-lock" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` | Before: only `docs/tasks/b31cab50-*/` hits. After: same, zero live hits |
186|| Tree cleanliness | `git status --short` / `git diff --stat` | Exactly one deleted file |
187|
188|The highest-risk validation step is **packaging after deletion (4.4)** — the
189|only step whose outcome cannot be fully predicted from the audit, since it
190|exercises the real tar + npm-closure path. If it fails, stop and diagnose
191|before claiming success; do not wave it through on the strength of the unit
192|suites.
193|
194|Manual check that cannot be automated: open the before/after `tar -tzf`
195|listings side by side and confirm the *only* entry difference is the missing
196|`runner/package-lock.json` line.
197|
198|## Documentation plan
199|
200|- **No live-doc edits are expected.** The audit found no live doc referencing
201|  the stub, so the implementation should change zero docs. If the Phase 1
202|  sweep surfaces a live reference, update or remove that mention and run
203|  `npm run docs:check` (link + JSDoc-example gates) to prove the docs tree is
204|  still consistent.
205|- **Historical reports stay untouched.** Do not edit the `b31cab50` review
206|  files or this plan's survey/idea inputs.
207|- **This plan file** (`docs/tasks/3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`)
208|  is the stage deliverable; no other docs artifact is required.
209|
210|## Risks and open questions
211|
212|- **Risk (low): a hidden consumer of the stub.** Mitigated by the Phase 1
213|  sweep plus the before/after packaging diff; the manifest-absence check
214|  makes an npm consumer impossible by construction.
215|- **Risk (low): suite-count drift.** The 182/182 figure is from the case
216|  study; suites may have grown since. The plan handles this by comparing
217|  before/after counts rather than pinning 182.
218|- **Risk (negligible): `dist/` pollution.** `dist/` is gitignored; scratch
219|  tarballs are deleted in steps 2.3 and 4.4 regardless.
220|- **Open questions: none.** The survey recorded no concerns, and every
221|  material fact (stub content, missing manifest, no install step, no live
222|  references, packaging behavior) was verified against the checkout. The only
223|  assumption is Key Decision 1's reading of "both runner test suites", which
224|  the plan covers by running both the cited pair and the full branch.
225|
226|## Non-goals
227|
228|- No changes to the packager, Dockerfile, publish flow, or any test.
229|- No new regression test asserting the file's absence (see Key Decision 3).
230|- No cleanup of other cruft, no `.gitignore` additions, no version bump
231|  (`runner/version.json` is untouched — this is not a runner release).

Task: `3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`
Date: 2026-11-17
Stage: retrospective (docs-only; follow-on ticket fan-out)

## History review

The ticket deleted one 6-line / 85-byte stub file (`runner/package-lock.json`,
a lockfile with no sibling `runner/package.json`). The file was inert but
had a long history of wasting agent attention:

- It was flagged in **three** separate reviews of case-study task
  `b31cab50-3ece-4678-a933-3192288fbefd` (update-impact review, PR review,
  final re-verification) and left in place as out of scope each time.
- Removing it then required its own full-pipeline ticket: a survey round, a
  231-line implementation plan for a 1-file deletion, two full CI cycles
  (one ~43-minute run ending in a canary infra flake), and a PR review.
- Both CI cycles failed on causes unrelated to the change (see below); the
  task's own gates (packaging + runner suites) were green throughout.

## Where agent effort went (difficulties and fails)

1. **No guard against the file class.** Nothing in the repo stops an orphan
   lockfile (or any stray file under `runner/`) from landing in git or
   shipping in the release tarball: `scripts/package-runner.mjs`
   (`copyPruned`) copies the whole `runner/` tree except a small
   forbidden-name list, and no test pins the tarball file list. Every agent
   auditing the runner packaging path had to re-derive inertness from
   scratch. Structural fix, prevents recurrence entirely.
2. **Unrelated canary infra flake burned a full cycle.** CI run 1 failed with
   all 13 fast branches green and canary at 139/140: `footer-overlay` died
   in `page.goto` with "Target page, context or browser has been closed"
   (resource exhaustion on the shared gate host). ~43 minutes lost on a
   ticket touching no UI code.
3. **Unrelated frontend unit flake burned the retry.** CI run 2 failed
   `Unit Tests (frontend)` on one assertion out of 4791
   (`ProjectSettings.test.jsx` harness-combobox `not.toBeDisabled()`),
   on branch content identical to run 1 where frontend passed. One flaky
   assertion failed the fast gate and skipped canary. Run 2 also
   reinstalled frontend deps (535 packages) while run 1 was "up to date",
   so dependency drift is a second hypothesis alongside async timing.
4. **Minor: acceptance phrasing needed interpretation.** "Both runner test
   suites" did not name exact commands (plan covered it by running both the
   cited pair and the full 20-file branch), and "no reference remains in
   docs" needed an explicit exception for immutable history under
   `docs/tasks/`. Handled in-plan; not worth a ticket on its own.

## Dedupe check (KainBain)

Resolved project `0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a` (kainbain),
workflow `wf-default`, target stage `1` (Idea). Current task sits in
`stage-1794594754686` (retrospective), so targeting stage `1` respects the
recursion guard. Listed all 67 tasks in `wf-default`:

- Difficulty 2 (canary resource-exhaustion flake) already has open ticket
  `984cc6f6-9d8a-48dc-ab8a-d9dff944a3bf` in stage `1` with substantially
  the same goal (same spec, same error class). **Not duplicated.**
- The general quarantine lane + failure attribution already exists via
  completed ticket `8769b002-02e5-4e7d-8779-24865192d57c`.
- No open ticket covers orphan lockfiles / stray tarball entries or the
  ProjectSettings flake. **Two tickets created (cap: 10).**

Note: the skill's default API base `http://localhost:3100` refused
connections from this runner checkout (no local listener); all calls used
the runner backend `http://192.168.1.206:3100` from the runner env, which
serves the live orchestrator data.

## Tickets created

| Ticket | Title | Stage | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2c1414d8-92ae-4ecc-9018-c3d4ca8a564d` | Fail CI on orphan package-lock.json files and stray runner tarball entries | `1` (Idea) | waiting_human |
| `8d41bf8c-f21d-4b3c-84d7-cd8891edddb0` | Quarantine and root-cause the ProjectSettings harness-combobox disabled flake | `1` (Idea) | waiting_human |

Both created with `execute: false` and deterministic idempotency keys, and
both verified via re-read to sit in `currentStageId: 1`. Each goal is
self-contained (problem, fix, success criteria) and cites this task
(`3232f6c6-9d02-4654-8d08-1a3fa27ab403`) as its case study with evidence
paths, so a human reviewer can audit either ticket with zero extra context.

- Ticket `2c1414d8` (difficulty 1): fast gate failing on any
  `package-lock.json` without a sibling `package.json`, plus a
  `package-runner-conformance` assertion that no lockfile ships under
  `runner/`. Prevents the entire ticket class.
- Ticket `8d41bf8c` (difficulty 3): quarantine the ProjectSettings flake in
  the lane from `8769b002`, then root-cause timing vs dep drift. Explicitly
  scoped to exclude the canary flake (owned by `984cc6f6`).

## Deliberately not ticketed

- Canary footer-overlay resource-exhaustion flake: covered by open ticket
  `984cc6f6` (dedupe, see above).
- Acceptance-phrasing nits (difficulty 4): absorbed by the plan's key
  decisions; too small for a standalone ticket.
- A "trivial-change fast lane" for the pipeline: considered, but speculative
  process design with lower reliability than the two concrete fixes above;
  the orphan-lockfile guard already removes this ticket class entirely.
